documents.text:
Netherwood - commissioning snag summary

December 2024 (compiled retrospectively - weekly records
incomplete for Oct/Nov)

Energisation achieved 09/12/2024, against a baseline of
30/09/2024. Total slip approximately 10 weeks.

Principal causes, in order of impact:

1. Planning condition discharge (6 weeks). Construction traffic
   management plan delayed by the civils contractor. Start on
   site pushed accordingly.

2. Transformer delivery (3 weeks). Supplier revised lead time
   after order placed.

3. Commissioning snags (1 week). Various, mostly minor. Notable:
   PCS firmware was not updated consistently across all units
   during snagging - one unit was offline during the update window
   and was missed. This was not picked up at handover.

LESSONS
The first two causes were both visible months in advance and
neither was formally escalated until they had already bitten. Our
weekly reports recorded them as "issues" from early on but there
is no mechanism that turns a repeated issue into an escalation.

Handover documentation to Operations was incomplete. The firmware
point above was known to the commissioning team and did not make
it into the handover pack.
documents.title: Netherwood commissioning snag summary

documents.text:
NETHERWOOD - HANDOVER TO OPERATIONS
Status as at 20/01/2025

Energisation: 09/12/2024
Handover meeting: 18/12/2024
Status: INCOMPLETE

Outstanding items:

- As-built drawings: issued but not verified against site. Two
  discrepancies already found by Operations in the cable route.
- O&M manuals: received for PCS and HVAC, outstanding for the BMS.
- Commissioning records: partial. Some test sheets missing.
- Firmware versions: not formally recorded at handover. Operations
  have since found at least one PCS on an earlier version than the
  rest of the site.
- Spares inventory: not provided.
- Training: two sessions delivered, a third outstanding.

COMMENT
Operations have accepted the site into service because commercially
we needed to start delivering, but the handover is not complete and
the outstanding items are now competing with live operational work
for attention.

This is the third site in a row where handover has been signed off
as "complete with exceptions" and the exceptions have then taken
months to close out.
documents.title: Netherwood handover to Operations status

documents.text:
# Netherwood - Lessons learned workshop

**Date:** 5 February 2025
**Attendees:** Project delivery, Development, Operations,
Procurement

## What went well
- Construction quality, no significant defects
- Site team / contractor relationship
- HSE record: zero reportable incidents

## What did not

**1. Early warnings were recorded but not escalated.**
Both the planning condition delay and the transformer lead time
appear in weekly reports weeks or months before they affected the
programme. Nobody connected the repetition. The weekly report
format records issues but has no concept of "this is the fifth
week running".

**2. Contractor performance information is not shared between
projects.**
The civils contractor's delay at Netherwood was not known to the
Drumgarve team when they were appointed there.

**3. Handover was incomplete.**
See separate handover status note. Operations inherited open items
with no clear owner.

## Agreed actions
1. Introduce a formal escalation trigger for repeated issues -
   owner: project delivery. **Status at time of writing: not done.**
2. Share contractor performance notes across projects - owner:
   procurement. **Status: not done.**
3. Handover checklist with sign-off - owner: operations.
   **Status: drafted.**
documents.title: Netherwood lessons learned workshop

documents.text:
DRUMGARVE BESS - PROCUREMENT ISSUE

Date raised: 2025-02-07
Raised by: Procurement
Project: Drumgarve (40MW)

Main transformer lead time has been revised by the supplier from
38 weeks to 54 weeks. Notified by email 05/02, no advance warning.

This pushes delivery from September 2025 to January 2026.

IMPACT
Energisation forecast moves from Nov 2025 to Mar 2026, a slip of
approximately 16 weeks. Drumgarve does not currently hold a
capacity market agreement so the direct revenue exposure is lower
than it would be at Ashfield, but we lose a winter of trading
revenue.

OPTIONS CONSIDERED
1. Accept the revised date
2. Source from an alternative supplier - lead times quoted
   between 45 and 60 weeks, so no benefit
3. Second-hand / ex-stock unit - one identified, specification
   does not match

RECOMMENDATION
Accept and replan. Also: this is the second transformer lead time
extension from this supplier in 14 months (see Netherwood, Dec
2023). We should stop treating their quoted lead times as firm
and build contingency into the programme at the point of order,
not when they tell us.
documents.title: Drumgarve transformer lead time issue

Drumgarve site visit - notes
30 May 2025

Pre-construction walkover with the civils contractor and the
landowner.

Points noted:

- Access track from the B-road is narrower than the drawings
  indicate at two pinch points. Will not accommodate a container
  delivery without widening. Contractor says "we'll manage" - I
  am not convinced. Same issue caused a second crane visit at
  Ashfield.

- Drainage: standing water at the northern end of the site after
  recent rain. Ground investigation report did not flag this.
  Worth a second look before foundation design is finalised.

- Landowner raised the hedgerow removal timing. Nesting season
  restrictions may affect the planned start date. Not currently
  in the programme risk register.

- Contractor has not yet provided the swept path analysis for the
  traffic management condition. Chased on site.

General impression: site is workable but there are three or four
things here that are not in the risk register and should be.

documents.text:
# Drumgarve - Planning condition discharge status

**Date:** 12 June 2025
**Author:** A. Lindqvist, Development

## Summary

Seven pre-commencement conditions, five discharged. Two
outstanding:

**Condition 9 (landscaping and screening)**
Submitted 14/04. Local authority requested additional detail on
species selection 02/05. Revised submission 19/05. No response
since. 8 weeks elapsed against a statutory 8 week determination.

**Condition 14 (construction traffic management)**
Not yet submitted. Requires a swept path analysis from the civils
contractor, who have not provided it despite three requests. This
is blocking.

## Risk

Condition 14 is pre-commencement. We cannot start on site until
it is discharged. Programme assumes start 01/08. If the
contractor does not provide the analysis within two weeks that
date is at risk.

## Note

The same contractor was late providing equivalent information at
Netherwood in 2024, which cost us six weeks there. This is a
pattern, not a one-off, and it should be reflected in how we
contract with them.
documents.title: Drumgarve planning condition discharge status

PM: M. Reilly

PROGRAMME
Baseline energisation 30/11/2025
Current forecast 20/03/2026 (transformer)
Status: in delay

PROGRESS
Pre-construction only. Site not yet started - blocked on planning
condition 14.

ISSUES
- Condition 14 still not discharged. Civils contractor has not
  provided the swept path analysis. Fourth request sent 11/06.
- Condition 9 overdue for determination with the LPA.
- Transformer delivery Jan 2026 confirmed.
- Access track pinch points (raised at the May walkover) not yet

- Hedgerow / nesting season constraint not yet assessed.

The transformer is the binding constraint so the planning delays
are not currently costing us programme. That will change if the
transformer date improves or if conditions remain outstanding into
the autumn.

documents.author: J. Patel
documents.text:
Ashfield weekly - week ending 04/07/2025

PM: J. Patel

PROGRAMME
Baseline energisation 14/11/2025
Current forecast 28/11/2025 - FORECAST SLIPPED 14 DAYS
Float: zero, now in delay

PROGRESS
Mechanical and electrical installation complete. Site is
effectively ready for energisation.

ISSUES
DNO have now confirmed the connection works date: 10/11/2025.
This leaves no contingency before the 14/11 energisation date and
the works themselves are quoted at 5-10 working days.

This has been flagged in weekly reports since March. The date was
never confirmed and we did not escalate it formally. In hindsight
we should have, in week 12.

Commercial implication: we have a capacity market agreement with
a delivery start of 01/12/2025. A 14 day slip takes us to 28/11,
which is inside the window but with nothing spare. Any further
slip and we are exposed.

ACTIONS
- Formal escalation to DNO account manager (done 03/07)
- Reviewing whether any commissioning activity can be brought
  forward

documents.text:
Ashfield - DNO correspondence summary
Compiled 10/07/2025 by J. Patel

Chronology of contact regarding final connection works date:

06/02/2025 - Initial request for programme. Acknowledged.
06/03/2025 - Chased. No response.
04/04/2025 - Chased. Holding reply, "with the programming team".
09/05/2025 - Chased. Verbal: "late summer", nothing written.
11/06/2025 - Chased. No response.
26/06/2025 - DNO issue date: 10/11/2025.
03/07/2025 - Formal escalation to account manager.

Five chases over five months before a date was issued, and the
date issued leaves no contingency.

Observation: each chase was recorded in the relevant weekly
report as an issue, but because each week it looked like a single
unanswered email, it never read as urgent. Seen together the
pattern is obvious.
